description: The local windows: the main one (`home`, the editor's shell on a folder of this computer) and each folder's or document's (`files-*`), local content served from the app's own bundle. They may call what their shell and its This device view call: this computer's recent places and pointing a window at another, who is signed in and the account's sandboxes as the workspace last told them, and the way to them, the account's own platform calls (its menu and Settings: a short list account.rs checks, sent by the app with the workspace's session, which the page never holds), a sandbox for the window's own folder (project.rs: what its dialog draws, and the window's folder put in line for a sandbox of its own, never a folder the page names; folder_setup.rs: each folder's setup as it goes, and, for the window's own folder only, trying again, putting it away, the restart its setup asks for), and the machine's sandboxes, agent, Docker engine (which engine the sandboxes run on, and the move to the other: engine.rs), on Intentic OS the OS itself and the changes to it (os.rs: each one `ic os` verb) and this computer's network, sound, screens, keyboard and drives (os_settings.rs: each one `ic os` verb, a Wi-Fi password on its stdin), setups (a fresh code for one whose own ran out included, minted with the workspace's session as a folder's own sandbox's is) and syncs, the machine agents of this computer's other environments (agents.rs: which WSL distro runs one, read off their files), the keyring on this computer, the Passwords view (keyring.rs: each one `intentic-machine keyring` verb, the Passwords app's input on stdin), and what this computer's own AI tools say (found.rs: the subscriptions signed in here by who they are for, never a token, and the folders their histories name). The documents they draw can call none of it: the page's policy runs no script but the bundle's own (vite.local.config.ts), frames a document opens are other origins with no capability, and a link from a local window is heard only as `window` or `local` (setup_link.rs). The workspace is remote content and gets nothing at all: its only channel into the app is the intentic:// navigation the window handler intercepts. Named by WEBVIEW, not by window: the main window is a webview in the app's one window beside the workspace (frame.rs), and a capability naming that window would grant all of this to the workspace's remote page too. A local window titles itself through the app (`local_title`), never with `set-title`: in the one window that would retitle the workspace as well. Every command of the app's own is a permission granted here by name (build.rs).
